speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You are presenting with double vision, difficulty climbing stairs, and upper limb weakness. To understand the pattern of your neurological deficits, can you tell me if your double vision goes away when you close one eye, and are these symptoms getting worse over time?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis. The combination of diplopia triggered by vertical gaze and fluctuating weakness that worsens with exertion and improves with rest is classic for this condition. I will not order further imaging as the clinical presentation is highly specific.
